text: So it's not something that we can decide, or the manufacturer can decide. It's given by the standard, and the standard as set this time slot duration based on the, let's say, fraction of sensing time. Okay, remember the sensing time. We said we used the physical layer to sense the power of the channel and then to compute an energy to see if the channel is idle or busy. Okay, so this is essentially this fraction of time, and this is essentially the minimum to sense the power on the on the channel and the physical layer, plus the time that is needed by the transceiver to switch from transmit mode to receive mode or vice versa. That's called turnaround time of the transceiver. So this is detail, but what is important to keep in mind is that as we know, Wi-Fi cards are half duplex, so they have to use the only transceiver they have got to transmit or to receive, right? So when they are transmitting at a certain point, they finish transmitting, they may need to switch into receive mode. Well, this happens, for example, when we apply stop and wait. Remember how stop and wait works. You transmit a packet, and then you are supposed to receive.
